To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) interactive visualizations that enable users to interact with recommen- dation systems can increase the likelihood of nding interesting items and that (b) personalizing both visualizations and user controls to di erent user characteristics can further increase this likelihood.

1) interactive recommender systems that allow users to steer the recommender system process are promising for increasing the nding rate of relevant items; 2) the e ectiveness of these systems is dependent on the personal characteristics of the user; 3) the design of recommender systems that incorporate user controls and interactive visualizations should take personal characteristics into account.

“The design of recommender systems should take into account the personal characteristics of end-users, and provide them with personalized visualizations and control elements to enhance the user experience.”
